events.boundary: Ada Lovelace's lifecycle, 10 December 1815 to 27 November 1852.
events.description: Only legitimate child of Lord Byron and Annabella Milbanke; raised by her mother on a regime of mathematics meant to keep her father out of her; paralysed after measles 1829-31; met Babbage 5 June 1833; married William King 8 July 1835; children 1836, 1837, 1839; Countess 1838; calculus with De Morgan by letter from 1840; translated Menabrea and wrote the Notes in 1843. In this world, from August 1843 she conducts the business of the engines under the Book of Conditions, raises a subscription among the assurance offices and sees a table engine built; she dies of uterine cancer in November 1852, as historically.
provenance: source: era package to Aug 1843; invented after

events.boundary: Charles Babbage's lifecycle, 26 December 1791 to 18 October 1871.
events.description: Banker's son; Cambridge and the Analytical Society 1812; married Georgiana Whitmore 1814, who died in 1827, the year his father died and left him a fortune; the Difference Engine from 1823 on public money; Lucasian Professor 1828-39; the Analytical Engine from 1834; government support ended 1842. In this world he accepts negotiated conditions from Lovelace in 1843, turns his designing to an engine that can be built and finished, and after her death returns to the Analytical Engine until he dies in 1871, as historically.
provenance: source: era package to Aug 1843; invented after

events.boundary: History as it touches The Book of Conditions: Britain and its correspondents, 1779-1918. Real history up to 15 August 1843; after that, the authored branch in which Babbage negotiates Lovelace's conditions.
events.description: The accepted world of the novel. Up to the morning of 15 August 1843 it follows the record in the era package; from then on it is invented, and real lives the change would not touch are kept as they were.

Griffith Davies's lifecycle, 5 December 1788 to 21 March 1855.
upsert.description: Born at Llandwrog in Caernarfonshire to a poor family; worked young, taught himself mathematics, came to London about 1809, taught and then kept his own school; actuary to the Guardian Assurance Company from 1823, whose success was credited to his tables; twenty-four reports on life contingencies and FRS in 1831. In this world, from 1844 he is the bridge between the engines and the assurance offices, trustee of the subscription and the engine's first customer. He dies in March 1855, as historically.
provenance: source: era package; inferred early details; invented after 1843

upsert.boundary: Enoch Dunn's lifecycle, August 1818 to March 1896 (invented).
upsert.description: Born in Bolton, son of a handloom weaver ruined by the power loom; Methodist Sunday school; apprenticed to a millwright at fourteen; came to Whitworth's Chorlton Street works in 1837 and became one of its best fitters. In this world Whitworth sends him in 1848 to erect the table engine in London; he stays.

upsert.boundary: Hester Fell's lifecycle, April 1811 to July 1884 (invented).
upsert.description: Born in Clerkenwell to a writing-and-arithmetic master who taught her logarithms at his elbow; married Thomas Fell, a law-stationer's clerk, in 1832; one surviving daughter, Kate (1834); widowed by typhus in 1840; supports herself by copying and by computing at piecework for out-of-house computers of the Nautical Almanac and for actuaries. In this world Griffith Davies employs her from 1844 to compute the check tables the engine must match, and she becomes the engine's verifier.

upsert.boundary: William King's lifecycle, 21 February 1805 to 29 December 1893.
upsert.description: Son of the 7th Baron King; Eton and Trinity, Cambridge; a secretary's post in the Ionian Islands; married Ada Byron 8 July 1835; Earl of Lovelace 1838; FRS 1841; Lord Lieutenant of Surrey; an amateur builder who rebuilt East Horsley in brick and bent timber. In this world his consent and signature carry the subscription his wife cannot legally sign, and the engine strains and then reshapes the marriage. He outlives her by forty-one years, remarries in 1865 and dies in 1893, as historically.
provenance: source: era package and general record; invented after 1843

upsert.boundary: George Biddell Airy's lifecycle, 27 July 1801 to 2 January 1892.
upsert.description: Born at Alnwick; Trinity, Cambridge, Senior Wrangler; Lucasian Professor before Babbage; Astronomer Royal from 1835 to 1881, an organiser of computation by human computers at Greenwich; in 1842 advised Peel's government that the Difference Engine was useless. His life runs as historically: in this world he is the engines' official sceptic, asked again in 1849 and 1851, and his judgment matters at two points.
provenance: source: era package; inferred career details

upsert.boundary: Lady Byron's lifecycle, 17 May 1792 to 16 May 1860.
upsert.description: Only child of Sir Ralph Milbanke; educated in mathematics (Byron's 'Princess of Parallelograms'); married Byron January 1815 and left him a year later with their month-old daughter; raised Ada under close supervision and a mathematical regime; reformer and founder of schools; managing, watchful and much consulted. In this world she opposes her daughter's business, then holds its money in reserve; her life otherwise runs as historically; she dies in 1860.

upsert.boundary: Joseph Clement's lifecycle, 13 June 1779 to 28 February 1844.
upsert.description: Born at Great Asby, Westmorland, a handloom weaver's son; weaver and slater, then loom-maker and self-taught draughtsman; with Bramah from 1814 and chief draughtsman at Maudslay's; his own workshop at 21 Prospect Place, Newington, from 1817; built the Difference Engine 1824-33 until the dispute over cost and the ownership of his tools; urged a standard screw thread in 1828. He dies in February 1844, as historically: the change does not reach his illness. In this world the negotiation over his drawings and the remaining engine parts is one of the first things Lovelace conducts.
provenance: source: era package; invented after Aug 1843

upsert.boundary: Augustus De Morgan's lifecycle, 27 June 1806 to 18 March 1871.
upsert.description: Born at Madurai, India; blind in one eye from infancy; Trinity, Cambridge, refused a fellowship for refusing the religious test; first professor of mathematics at University College London from 1828; married Sophia Frend 1837; consulting actuary and author on probability and life contingencies; taught Ada calculus by letter from about 1840; Formal Logic 1847. In this world he is named the umpire of the Book of Conditions in 1843, and his actuarial connections bring in Davies. Otherwise his life runs as historically; he dies in 1871.
provenance: source: era package; inferred career details; invented umpire role

upsert.description: Mary Somerville's elder son by her first husband, Samuel Greig; Cambridge; barrister of the Inner Temple; Ada's friend and confidant, who knew her and William from before the marriage. In this world he drafts the deed of trust through which a married woman can conduct a subscription she cannot legally sign. His life otherwise runs as historically.

upsert.boundary: Henry Prevost Babbage's lifecycle, 16 September 1824 to 29 January 1918.
upsert.description: Charles Babbage's youngest surviving son; schooled in London and taught drawing in his father's workshop; joined the Bengal Army of the East India Company and sailed for India late in 1843. His life runs as historically, since he had left before the business took form: service in India, the Mutiny years, retirement as a general, return to England, editing his father's papers on the engines (1889) and building a working portion of the Analytical Engine's mill. In this world the table engine and the Book of Conditions come to him after his father's death in 1871.
provenance: source: era package; inferred details; invented inheritance

upsert.boundary: Mary Somerville's lifecycle, 26 December 1780 to 29 November 1872.
upsert.description: Born in Jedburgh and raised at Burntisland; largely self-taught in mathematics against her family's wishes; widowed young from Samuel Greig, then married William Somerville; famous for Mechanism of the Heavens (1831) and On the Connexion of the Physical Sciences (1834); mentor to the young Ada; lived in Italy from 1838. Her life runs as historically: she is a correspondent at a distance in this story, and the change reaches her only by letter. She dies in Naples in 1872.

upsert.boundary: Joseph Whitworth's lifecycle, 21 December 1803 to 22 January 1887.
upsert.description: Born in Stockport; trained as a mechanic; in London with Maudslay, Holtzapffel and Clement, helping make the Difference Engine; his own machine-tool firm in Manchester from 1833; standard screw thread proposed 1841. In this world, his firm contracts in 1845 to make the table engine's calculating section to standard threads and planed surfaces; otherwise his life runs as historically, because the contract is one among many and does not change his firm's course: leading engineering works, rifles, a baronetcy, death in 1887.
provenance: source: era package; invented contract after 1844

upsert.description: Nine years without progress after the stoppage gave Airy and the Treasury their case.
The letter sets the terms Babbage answers on the morning of the 15th.
Having mastered the engine on paper, she has standing in her own eyes to offer more.
With the government gone, Babbage has no other route to building anything; this is what makes negotiating thinkable for him in this world.
provenance: invented: the cause of the divergence

upsert.description: The quarrel shows Ada that Babbage's public dealings ruin his cause; she answers it with an offer to manage them.

upsert.boundary: Babbage helps found the Analytical Society at Cambridge, 1812.
Annabella leaves Byron with the month-old Ada, January 1816.
upsert.description: Byron leaves England in April and never sees his daughter again. Ada grows up with her mother and her mother's account of her father.

upsert.boundary: Babbage helps found the Astronomical Society, 1820.
Griffith Davies becomes actuary to the Guardian Assurance Company, 1823.
provenance: inferred: era package says advisory actuary; date sketch

upsert.boundary: The government grants Babbage £1,700 to begin the Difference Engine, 1823.
Lord Byron dies at Missolonghi, April 1824; Ada is eight.
Clement begins building the Difference Engine in his workshop, 1824.
Babbage's year of deaths, 1827: his father in February, his wife Georgiana in September, and an infant son.
upsert.description: His inheritance makes him rich; the losses send him abroad for a year and fix his life thereafter on work and society rather than a household.
provenance: source: era package and general record

upsert.boundary: Babbage becomes Lucasian Professor of Mathematics at Cambridge, 1828-1839.

upsert.description: Nearly three years confined, much of it flat on her back; she learns to live inside her own head and her studies.

upsert.boundary: Babbage publishes Reflections on the Decline of Science in England, 1830.
Davies writes twenty-four reports on life contingencies and is elected FRS, 1831.
A working portion of the Difference Engine, about one seventh, is assembled, 1832.
Ada, seventeen, meets Babbage at a party at his house, 5 June 1833, and soon sees the Difference Engine demonstrated.
Work on the Difference Engine stops in a dispute with Clement over costs and the ownership of tools, 1833.
upsert.description: By the custom of the trade a workman kept the tools he made; Clement keeps them and the drawings stay in contention.

upsert.boundary: Whitworth sets up his own machine-tool firm in Manchester, 1833.
William King created Earl of Lovelace, June 1838; Ada becomes Countess.
The London and Birmingham Railway opens throughout, 1838.
De Morgan teaches Ada calculus, mostly by correspondence, 1840-1842.
Thomas Fell dies of typhus; Hester is widowed with a daughter of six, spring 1840 (invented).
upsert.description: She sells his books, moves to two rooms in Somers Town and takes in copying, then computing at piecework from a computer for the Nautical Almanac her father had known.

upsert.boundary: The Uniform Penny Post begins, January 1840.
Babbage explains the Analytical Engine at Turin at Plana's invitation, 1840.
Whitworth proposes a standard screw thread to the Institution of Civil Engineers, 1841.
Menabrea's account of the Analytical Engine published in French, October 1842.
Peel's government, advised by Airy, ends support for the engines; Babbage's meeting with Peel goes badly, November 1842.
Ada's sixteen-page letter to Babbage, 14 August 1843, offering to conduct the business of the engines on conditions.
upsert.description: She offers to 'conduct the business for you', with his 'own undivided energies being devoted to the execution of the work', on conditions she sets out.

upsert.boundary: The morning of 15 August 1843: Babbage sees Ada and does not refuse her conditions; he begins to negotiate (the divergence).
upsert.description: Historically he wrote on the letter that he saw her that morning and refused all the conditions. Here he reads them again, crosses out none, writes questions in the margin and asks for time. This is where the authored world departs from the record.
provenance: invented: the divergence named in the brief

upsert.boundary: Ada translates Menabrea and writes the Notes A to G, February to July 1843.
upsert.description: Six months of the hardest work of her life; Note G works out the Bernoulli numbers on the engine. She and Babbage write almost daily.

Babbage wants his unsigned preface on the government's failures published with the translation; Ada refuses; he proposes withdrawing the whole publication; she is furious. The translation appears without the preface.

upsert.boundary: The Analytical Engine as a design, 1834 onward.
upsert.description: Conceived 1834 as a general engine with a store, a mill and Jacquard cards; programs written 1837-40; explained at Turin 1840; Menabrea's account 1842; Lovelace's Notes 1843. Never built in Babbage's life historically; in this world its mill is partly built as the table engine's sibling.

upsert.boundary: The Book of Conditions, from its first page in September 1843 (invented).
upsert.description: A quarto notebook bound in green cloth, bought by Ada in Guildford. Each condition is written as an article; accepted articles carry both sets of initials; amendments are written beneath, and struck articles stay legible.
The kingdom in which tables are computed by hand, assurance offices multiply, machine shops train mechanics, the penny post and railways spread, and married women hold no property of their own.

upsert.boundary: Clement's workshop, 1817 to its sale after his death.
upsert.description: Built the Difference Engine 1824-33; famous for its large planing machine and fine work; the tools stayed with Clement after the 1833 dispute.

upsert.boundary: Difference Engine No. 1, from the 1823 grant to the end of the model.
upsert.description: Built by Clement 1824-33; a portion of about one seventh assembled in 1832, working with six digits and second differences; work stopped 1833; government support ended 1842 after more than £17,000. The portion was demonstrated in Babbage's drawing room for years.
The drawing room where the Difference Engine portion stood and the Saturday soirees met; the drawing office and workshop behind.
A London fire and life office whose success was credited largely to its actuary Griffith Davies's tables.
The King family's Surrey house, where Ada spent most of her married life outside the season.

upsert.boundary: Ada and her mother, from birth to Ada's death.
upsert.description: Close supervision in childhood, the 'Furies' who reported on her, a daughter who both feared and needed her mother's judgment. In this world the mother's opposition to the business turns, late, into its last resort.

upsert.boundary: The friendship of Ada and Babbage, 5 June 1833 to her death.
upsert.description: Begun at his party when she was seventeen; deepened through the Notes in 1843, when she called herself his fairy and he called her the Enchantress of Number; strained by the preface quarrel of August 1843. In this world it becomes a working partnership governed by the Book of Conditions.

upsert.boundary: The marriage of Ada and William King, courtship spring 1835 to her death.
upsert.description: A kind, practical, somewhat formal marriage; he admired and indulged her studies; she called him 'Crow'. In this world his name and signature carry the subscription, and its debts test the marriage.
Two rooms up one flight over a chandler's shop; a table by the window for the light; the New Road and the Euston terminus a few minutes south.

upsert.boundary: The Calculating Engine Subscription, from its deed in 1844 to its winding up (invented).
upsert.description: A trust, deed drawn by Woronzow Greig, with Griffith Davies and Augustus De Morgan as trustees and William King's signature where a married woman's could not stand; subscribers are assurance offices and private persons; its object is a table engine that computes and prints life tables.

upsert.boundary: The table engine, from first drawings to the end of the model (invented).
upsert.description: Drawn 1844-45 from Babbage's simplified second design under the Book of Conditions; parts made by Whitworth's in Manchester 1845-49; erected in London 1848-50; computing and printing life tables from 1850.
Founded 1833 in Chorlton Street, Manchester; planing machines, lathes, true planes and standard gauges; grew into one of the leading engineering works in Britain.

upsert.boundary: The first signed agreement in the Book of Conditions, Ockham Park, October 1843: what Babbage's undivided energies go to.
upsert.description: After six weeks of letters and two visits Ada and Babbage must write the first article that both initial: the object of the work. Babbage wants the Analytical Engine; Ada's letter asked for a definite thing that could be finished and paid for; Peel's refusal means no public money; Clement's parts and drawings sit in dispute in Newington. Weights are the modeler's proposal policy, set from those pressures: the table engine is likeliest because it has buyers (the assurance offices De Morgan knows) and a finishable scope; the mill is what Babbage's heart wants but has no buyer; finishing DE1 is blocked by Clement's tools and Babbage's distaste for the old design; drawings alone is the fallback if Ada's money plan fails.

answers.meaning: Build the Analytical Engine's mill as a demonstrable portion, to win a patron by showing it.
Build a table engine of simplified difference design, paid for by those who need tables, chiefly the life offices.
Recover Clement's parts and tools and finish Difference Engine No. 1.
Complete and publish the Analytical Engine drawings and notations; seek a builder later.

upsert.description: Only a buildable, finishable engine needs a maker.

upsert.boundary: Who makes the table engine's parts, decided in the spring of 1845.
upsert.description: By early 1845 the subscription has its first money and Babbage's drawings for the table engine's calculating section are nearly complete. Clement died in February 1844; his tools went to sale. Whitworth's Manchester works plane true surfaces and cut standard threads, and Whitworth had worked on the first engine as a young man; but Manchester is a day away by rail and Babbage will not be near the work. A workshop at Dorset Street would keep everything under Babbage's eye, which is exactly what Article the Third (on finishing) fears. Holtzapffel's is fine but small. Clement's former foreman could take on the old tools. Weights are the modeler's proposal policy.

upsert.boundary: Ada's first answer to the subscription's shortfall after the commercial crisis of October 1847.
upsert.description: The crisis of October 1847 ruins two private subscribers and makes one office withdraw its second instalment; the fund falls short of what Whitworth's next payment requires. Ada cannot sign or borrow in her own name. She has a mathematician's confidence in systems, a gambler's father, a circle of racing men among William's friends, a mother who would pay at a price, a husband who could raise money on the land, and the choice of cutting the printing apparatus. Weights are the modeler's proposal policy, set from those pressures; historically she did bet heavily on horses in 1848-51.

upsert.boundary: Article the First of the Book of Conditions, initialled at Ockham Park, October 1843: the object of the work is a table engine.
upsert.description: Babbage initials an article that names the object of his undivided energies: 'an engine of differences, of the new and simpler design, to calculate and print tables of mortality and of life annuities, and to be finished.' Ada's own clause, 'and to be finished', is the one he argues over longest. The Analytical Engine is named in a second article as the work that follows, not the work in hand.

answers.meaning: Whitworth's works, Chorlton Street, Manchester, to standard threads and planed surfaces; erected in London by a man Whitworth sends.
A workshop behind 1 Dorset Street with hired mechanics under Babbage's own eye.
Holtzapffel and Company, Charing Cross: fine work, small capacity.
Clement's former foreman, taking on the old tools after Clement's death.

upsert.description: The calculating section must run before the printer can be married to it.
Clement's promise brings his planer to the engine's account.
Failures in the crisis ruin two subscribers and frighten an office.
Davies agrees to be trustee and canvass the offices.
Only a trust can take the offices' money.
Her check tables bring her to the shop.
Six weeks of letters end in the first initialled article.
The redesign's waste and delay leave the fund without slack when the crisis comes.
Clement's planer makes a London shop possible.
With the shop eleven steps from his drawing board, Babbage can change what is being cut the same day.
The gap must be filled before Whitworth's next account and the men's wages.
Money in hand makes the choice of maker real.
Lady Byron's loan pays the shop through 1848-49.
The checking method is how the carry fault is found.
Barred from the business, she turns to the mathematics of checking.

upsert.boundary: Ada buys a green quarto notebook in Guildford and writes the first draft articles, mid-September 1843.
upsert.description: She writes the conditions out fair, one to a page, leaving the facing page blank for his objections. She calls it the Book of Conditions in a letter to Babbage, half in jest.

upsert.boundary: Henry Prevost Babbage sails for India to join the Bengal Army, late 1843.
The negotiation by letter and visit, 15 August to mid-October 1843.
upsert.description: Babbage answers her sixteen pages with eleven of his own: counter-conditions on his freedom of design, the ownership of drawings and his right to answer Airy in print. Two visits to Ockham; De Morgan proposed as umpire by Ada and accepted by Babbage because he respects De Morgan and De Morgan dislikes Airy.

upsert.boundary: Babbage's mother, Betty Plumleigh Babbage, dies, 1844.
upsert.description: She had kept his house since 1827. Month uncertain; placed at mid-year.
provenance: inferred: year from general record, month unknown

upsert.boundary: Clement's tools are sold; the great planing machine comes to the engine's account, summer 1844.
Ada visits the dying Clement at Prospect Place, January 1844.
upsert.description: Her first act of business. Clement, short of breath and proud, agrees to sell his great planing machine to the engine's account at his death and to let Babbage copy the Difference Engine drawings he holds. He tells her the engine stopped not for money but because Babbage would not stop changing it.

upsert.boundary: De Morgan brings Ada to Griffith Davies at the Guardian's office, April 1844.
upsert.description: Davies, a slate-quarry boy from Caernarfonshire who walked to London, has spent twenty years having tables computed and checked by hand. He asks two questions: what it will cost, and whether it can be wrong. Ada answers the second better than the first.

upsert.boundary: The deed of trust of the Calculating Engine Subscription is signed, June 1844.
upsert.description: Drawn by Woronzow Greig, because a married woman can neither contract nor hold the fund. Trustees: Griffith Davies and Augustus De Morgan; William, Earl of Lovelace, signs as guarantor of the first £500 and as the person in whose name his wife acts. Ada is named in a schedule as 'the conductor of the business', a title with no standing in law.

upsert.boundary: Davies engages Hester Fell to compute the check tables against which the engine will be tried, October 1844.
upsert.description: At sixpence a page of verified figures, more than the Almanac's computers pay her, she computes, from the Carlisle table, the annuity values the engine will one day print. She understands that she is computing her own replacement.

upsert.boundary: The subscription is canvassed among the life offices, July 1844 to spring 1845.
upsert.description: Davies carries the prospectus to the offices himself; seven subscribe, the Guardian first with £800. Private subscribers include Lady Lovelace's friends, never in her own name.

upsert.boundary: Enoch Dunn comes from Manchester as foreman of the Dorset Street shop, May 1845.
upsert.description: Whitworth lends him for two years at his Manchester wage plus lodging. He brings Whitworth's gauges and the habit of working to a standard; he has never been south of Birmingham.

upsert.boundary: The engine workshop is fitted up behind 1 Dorset Street, April 1845.
upsert.description: Clement's great planer, two Whitworth lathes and a Whitworth planer bought new, and a foreman lent from Manchester. Babbage can walk from his drawing office into the shop in eleven steps.

upsert.boundary: The Lovelaces take 6 Great Cumberland Place, 1846, a short walk from Dorset Street.
Hester brings the first bound check tables to the Dorset Street shop and meets Enoch Dunn, April 1846.
Peel's government falls after the repeal of the Corn Laws, June 1846; Russell takes office.
The redesign quarrel, March to May 1846.
upsert.description: With a third of the figure wheels cut, Babbage redesigns the carriage to a faster anticipating mechanism borrowed from the Analytical Engine's mill. Enoch stops the shop rather than cut to drawings he expects to be withdrawn. Ada invokes Article the Third (no alteration after metal is cut without the umpire's consent). De Morgan's award in May allows the new carriage but freezes everything else and charges the waste to Babbage's own purse.
After the railway mania, a run of failures among corn merchants and banks; the Bank Charter Act is suspended on 25 October.

upsert.boundary: Ada goes to her mother at Moore Place, Esher, and accepts Lady Byron's conditions, December 1847.
upsert.description: Lady Byron lends £2,500 to the trust through her own man of business, not to her daughter. Her conditions, written in her own hand on a single sheet: that Ada give up the conducting of the business to Mr Davies for two years; that she submit to Dr Locock's regimen; that the loan be secured on the engine itself. Ada pastes the sheet into the Book of Conditions and initials it. She tells William afterwards.

upsert.boundary: Two private subscribers fail and one office withholds its second instalment; the fund falls short by about £2,400, November 1847.
Ada withdraws from conducting the business; Davies conducts it, January 1848 to January 1850.
Cholera in London, autumn 1848 to autumn 1849; about 14,000 dead.
Revolutions across Europe, February to summer 1848; the Chartist meeting at Kennington, April.
Ada and Hester work out the Rule of Two Hands for checking the engine, spring to autumn 1848.
upsert.description: Barred from the business, Ada takes the mathematics no one has asked for: how anyone will know the engine's tables are right. With Hester, in Hester's rooms and at Great Cumberland Place, she devises checks by differencing the printed results and by independent computation at sampled arguments. Ada writes the method out; Hester proves it on her own figures.

upsert.boundary: Airy inspects the engine at the trustees' invitation, November 1849.
upsert.description: He watches it run for an hour, checks three figures, and writes that it computes, that its tables would cost more than computers' tables, and that 'whether it is wanted is another question'.

upsert.boundary: The calculating section completes its first full run of a difference table, September 1849.
Ada resumes conducting the business, January 1850.
The first printed table: life annuities at three per cent, July 1850; Hester finds a discrepancy at age 71 and Enoch traces it to a worn carry lever.
The printing and stereotyping apparatus is finished, June 1850.
Ada's illness declares itself: haemorrhages from the spring, and Dr Locock's finding of cancer of the womb, 1851.
The Great Exhibition in Hyde Park, 1 May to 15 October 1851.
Ada dies at 6 Great Cumberland Place, 27 November 1852, aged thirty-six.
Ada's last illness, 1852: pain, laudanum, and her mother's management of the sickroom.
Ada asks Babbage to be her executor, August 1852.
Charles Babbage dies at Dorset Street, 18 October 1871.
Mary Somerville dies at Naples, 29 November 1872.
Henry Prevost Babbage builds a working portion of the Analytical Engine's mill, 1880s to 1910.
William King, Earl of Lovelace, dies, 29 December 1893.

changes.value: The branch's history 1843-1918, realizing D2 (Dorset Street shop) and D3 (Lady Byron's conditions), with every real death kept at its historical date.
First whole-life pass on the nine slow processes of Ada, Babbage, Davies and William: record-based to August 1843, invented after, every turn tied to an Event.

changes.value: Babbage's wants over his life. Carve: engines (to build his calculating engines), vindication (to be proved right against the government, Airy and the Royal Society's men), company (society, admiration, his Saturday evenings), family (his children and his mother), independence (to answer to no one, above all in design). Routing check: the unsigned preface (vindication), the redesign of 1846 (engines against independence), the soirees (company) each found one home.

A working engine makes the Exhibition a real question.

upsert.boundary: Whether and how the table engine goes to the Great Exhibition, decided January to March 1851.
upsert.description: The engine has printed its first table; the Commissioners offer space in the Machinery Court on their terms of placement and attendance. Babbage historically quarrelled with the Commission and wrote against the Exhibition; the Guardian wants its engine computing; Enoch fears the move to Hyde Park and back; Ada, returned as conductor, wants the engine seen. Weights are the modeler's proposal policy.

upsert.boundary: To whom Ada gives the Book of Conditions in her last months, summer 1852.
upsert.description: Dying, with her mother managing the sickroom and her husband estranged after her confession, Ada must decide what becomes of the green notebook that holds every condition she and Babbage signed and her mother's pasted sheet. Weights are the modeler's proposal policy.

upsert.boundary: What Hester and Enoch do once the engine is in service, early 1853.
upsert.description: Enoch's loan from Whitworth has long run out; he stayed on the subscription's wage. Hester is the engine's verifier. They have walked together since 1848. Kate Fell is nineteen. Weights are the modeler's proposal policy.

upsert.description: Henry inherits the engine; the Book can go where the engine is.
After the confession, the Book is what she can give him.
Hester has watched the law give a countess's work a schedule and no name; she will not give her own wages to a husband.
William reads the new law as a judgment on the old one, and on the Book.

upsert.boundary: Ada, already bleeding, comes to the Machinery Court on a June morning before the crowds and watches a page printed.
The jurors award the table engine a Council Medal, October 1851.
upsert.description: The medal is struck in Babbage's name alone; the jurors' report names the Calculating Engine Subscription and 'the Countess of Lovelace, who conducted its business', and does not name the foreman or the verifier.

upsert.boundary: The table engine in the Machinery Court of the Great Exhibition, May to October 1851, printing a page of life annuities each afternoon.
upsert.description: Ada, back as conductor, carries the Commissioners' terms through the Book of Conditions: Article the Third binds Babbage to the engine as it stands, and De Morgan's third award settles placement. Enoch and two men take it to Hyde Park in pieces and erect it in nine days. Crowds watch the printed page come out; Hester, in a grey dress, checks each afternoon's sheet against her own figures at a table beside it, and is mistaken by visitors for part of the exhibit.

upsert.boundary: Ada tells William something in August 1852 that makes him leave the room; the record does not say what.
upsert.description: Historically something passed between them in August 1852 that estranged William. This world keeps it unknown. What the model holds is its effect: his trust and closeness fall, and she turns to the Book.
provenance: inferred: general record; content left unknown

upsert.boundary: The table engine is installed in a back room of the Guardian's Lombard Street office, January 1852.
Ada writes the last article of the Book of Conditions and gives the Book to William, September 1852.
upsert.description: Article the Last, in a hand that wanders: that the husband who owns this book by law shall own it also by gift; that he shall read every page, including her mother's sheet; and that he shall do with it what he thinks right after she is dead. She does not ask him to forgive her. She initials it; there is no one to initial it beside her, and she leaves the space.

upsert.boundary: Enoch Dunn returns to Manchester as a foreman at Whitworth's, April 1853.
Enoch asks Hester to marry him and come north; she refuses, February 1853.
upsert.description: Whitworth offers Enoch a foremanship at Chorlton Street. Hester will not leave Kate or her work, and will not marry: under coverture her wages as the engine's verifier, the first money she has earned in her own right as more than a pair of hands, would become her husband's. She tells him this plainly. He says he would never touch it. She says the law would.

upsert.boundary: The Guardian returns the table engine to Babbage at Dorset Street, 1867, when the offices go over to the new tables of the Institute of Actuaries.
The Married Women's Property Act, 1870: a married woman keeps her own earnings.

Horsley Towers, spring 1878: William, seventy-three, gives the Book of Conditions to Henry Prevost Babbage, who has the engine and his father's papers at Dorset Street; Hester Fell, sixty-seven, comes at William's request to read the tables in it.
upsert.description: William has kept the Book twenty-five years and read it, as she asked, every page. After Babbage's death and the Act of 1870, he decides it belongs with the engine. Hester, who has never seen the Book, finds her own name in two articles.

upsert.boundary: Hester Fell dies in Somers Town, July 1884 (invented).
Enoch Dunn dies in Manchester, March 1896 (invented).

changes.value: Realize D4 (shown and works), D5 (the Book to William) and D6 (Enoch goes north; Hester stays), with the engine's later history and the coda.
Lives after 1852 as the draws made them (Hester stays, Enoch goes north, the Book with William, the medal), and values at the Events the earlier pass passed over.

Record how the story's processes drive one another. Redesign drives cost and waste; the Book and the umpire constrain redesign; money constrains making; coverture constrains Ada's authority and Hester's marriage; the engine's progress moves Hester's fear, Davies's credence and Airy's regard; Ada's workload drives her doses and her doses her body.

upsert.boundary: The table engine's calculating section, cut and erected at Dorset Street, May 1845 to September 1849.
upsert.description: Three columns of figure wheels, about 270 wheels in all, each gauged go and not-go for pitch, bore, boss and thickness; from 1846 the anticipating carriage, which lifts every carry in a column at once and makes each turn of the handle about half as long again as fast. Capacity: a table to seven figures and third differences. Limit: a worn carry lever can take a carry it should not, only when the figures fall just so.

upsert.boundary: The worn carry lever on the sixth wheel, found July 1850.
upsert.description: Hester's differencing finds the third differences jump at age 71; Enoch traces it to a bright flat on the lever's nose, no wider than a hair, worn by ten thousand turns. The lever had passed the gauge a year before; the steel wore. The failure mode the Rule of Two Hands exists to catch.

upsert.boundary: The table engine's printing and stereotyping apparatus, finished June 1850.
upsert.description: A train of type wheels presses each result into soft papier-mache, line under line; a plate is cast in type metal from the mould, so no compositor stands between engine and page. Thirty-one type wheels rejected, nineteen for dirty Sheffield steel.

changes.value: Give the table engine a life: its parts, capacities, limits and failure mode, as the chapters render them, and place the story's Events in the engine's, the Book's and the houses' lives.

upsert.description: Davies's credence, earned page by page in this room, lets the office take the engine.
The growing gap is what Ada must answer in 1847.

upsert.boundary: The Analytical Engine held as 'the next', 1845 to 1871.
upsert.description: Conceived 1834; described in the Notes of 1843. Under the Book's terms its design is not frozen and not built: it waits on the table engine's proving that an engine can earn. Babbage goes on drawing it at night against the article that keeps his days for the table engine. Capacity on paper: a store and a mill, operation cards and variable cards, conditional branching. Limit: no workshop on earth can yet hold its tolerances at its size, and no purse its cost. It is never built.

upsert.boundary: The Book of Conditions as an object, autumn 1843 to April 1878.
upsert.description: A green cloth quarto with a leather spine, bought for 4s. 6d. (the price inked inside the front board). First leaf: Between C.B. and A.A.L., with A. De M. as umpire. Every article to be initialled by both. Nothing binds that is not written here. Parts: the articles in Ada's hand, Clement's memorandum under a gummed strip, the coverture page (What the law says I am / What this book says I am), De Morgan's award of 284 pounds 6 shillings, Lady Byron's pasted sheet of three conditions, the Rule of Two Hands, the jurors' page in Davies's hand, the last page with its space for the other's initials. Swollen to half again its thickness by pastings. Capacity: binds only what both initial. Limit: it cannot bind anyone who has not initialled, cannot give Ada a legal person, and holds nothing for the illness; its failure mode is the blank beside a single set of initials.

upsert.boundary: The Book locked in William's desk at Horsley, November 1852 to April 1878.
upsert.description: Given to William by Ada when dying, with the charge to read every page and do what he thought right. He reads it over three evenings in December 1852 and for twenty-five years does nothing with it, because he does not know what is right.

upsert.boundary: Difference Engine No. 1's finished portion, 1832 onward.
upsert.description: About one-seventh of the engine, assembled by Clement in 1832: a demonstration piece that calculates but does not print. The work stopped in 1833 over Clement's claim to the tools and his costs for moving to Dorset Street. Failure mode: a design that changed under the maker's hands, paid for by a Treasury that could not see the end of it. Its lesson is the table engine's first article: freeze the design.

upsert.boundary: The Guardian as the engine's keeper, 1852 to 1867.
upsert.description: The office takes the table engine when the trust can no longer carry it, prints its tables under the Rule of Two Hands with Hester as second hand, and gives it up in 1867 for the Institute of Actuaries' hand-computed tables, back to Henry Babbage. It keeps Hester computing three days a week into the 1870s.

upsert.boundary: Davies's table room at the back of the Guardian's office, Lombard Street, second floor, 1823 onward.
upsert.description: North light over the roofs that never falls on the paper. Here the office's tables are computed and checked by paid men, and still found in error; here Davies writes the £800 subject-to note in 1845, and here Hester's pages come by clerk's parcel. Capacity: an actuary's judgement trusted by the directors without question. Limit: hand computation, checked by hand, with errors that survive both.

upsert.boundary: The life-office subscription raised, February to May 1845.
upsert.description: Seven offices subscribe by the end of May; the Guardian's £800, subject to independent check tables under Davies, a frozen design and a trust, is the largest share; the smallest is £150 from a Norwich office that pays late and in full. Capacity: money without the Treasury and without Babbage's name at its head. Limit: a fixed sum raised once, against a cost that grows with every change and every turn of the bank rate.

upsert.boundary: The subscription's shortfall, April to November 1847.
upsert.description: Davies, going through the ledger with the subscription book and Enoch's weekly returns, makes the shortfall to the finish about £1,400 before the panic and about £2,400 after it. Failure mode: the subscribers are themselves life offices whose funds the panic squeezes, so the money fails exactly when it is needed.

changes.value: Lives for the Book, the Guardian, the subscription, the Analytical Engine and Difference Engine No. 1: parts, capacities, limits, failure modes and histories, as the chapters render them.

upsert.description: The street in the story's years.
The house in the Lovelaces' years.
The house in the Lovelaces' years.

upsert.boundary: Britain, 1843 to 1852: railway mania, the panic of 1847, cholera, the Exhibition.
upsert.description: Railway mania 1845 to 1846 draws capital away from everything else; the commercial crisis of 1847 and the Bank Act suspended on 25 October 1847; cholera in London 1848 to 1849; the Great Exhibition 1851 with the table engine in the Machinery Court. Life offices multiply and need tables. The era's money is cheap and then suddenly dear, and the engine's subscription lives inside that swing.

upsert.boundary: Clement's works, Prospect Place, Southwark, 1817 to 1844.
upsert.description: The finest shop in London for plane surfaces and screws; trained Whitworth. Built the portion of Difference Engine No. 1, and claimed the special tools as his own when the work stopped in 1833. Failure mode, for Babbage: a maker who owns his tools owns the work's pace.

upsert.boundary: Great Cumberland Place: the Lovelaces' London house from 1846.
upsert.description: Where Ada keeps the engine's business from 1846: the ledger, the subscription book and the green Book in the drawing room. Lady Byron comes here on 4 November 1847 to hear the whole of the shortfall. Affords: a countess's address for a business no countess may legally conduct.

upsert.boundary: Dorset Street, Marylebone: Babbage's house and the shop behind it, 1829 to 1878.
upsert.description: Babbage's house, where his Saturday evenings fill the drawing room, with the fireproof shop at the back built for Difference Engine No. 1. From 1845 it is the table engine's shop under Enoch: a planer, lathes, the gauge board, the wheel rack on the wall, the ledger Hester keeps. Affords: the designer within a staircase of the work, which is both its strength and the way redesign gets in. In 1867 the engine comes back to stand in the coach house.

upsert.boundary: Lombard Street, City of London: the street of banks and life offices, 1840s to 1850s.
upsert.description: The Guardian's office is here, and the banks whose discount rate rules the subscribers' funds. Enoch walks up from here to Chalton Street in 1852. Affords: credit, actuarial judgement, notice of panic the same afternoon.

upsert.boundary: Ockham Park, Surrey: the Lovelaces' country house, 1835 onward.
upsert.description: William's building, his estate, the children's house. Where Ada's August 1843 letter is written. Affords distance from London and the work; for Ada it is both rest and exile.

upsert.boundary: Ada and her mother: the three conditions, November 1847 to Ada's death.
upsert.description: Lady Byron hears the whole of the shortfall, asks eleven exact questions, goes through the ledger with her finger, and offers money on three written conditions pasted into the Book with her initials. Her help is real and is control: the relationship's lifelong form, now on paper.

upsert.boundary: Ada and Babbage under the Book, 1843 to 1852.
upsert.description: Phases: negotiation (autumn 1843, articles argued word by word); partnership and quarrel (1845 to 1846, the redesign quarrel, Ada's anger, De Morgan's award); her withdrawal (1848) and return (1850); he is not asked to come when she is dying (1852). Each holds something the other needs and cannot command: his engine, her business. The Book is how they trust without trusting.

upsert.boundary: Ada and William: the deed signed in the Strand, 1844, to her death.
upsert.description: To let the trust name Ada as its business agent at all, William signs in a lawyer's chambers in the Strand for a wife who does not exist in law; she holds his hand from the Strand to Charing Cross and no farther. Phases: consent given against his pride, his silence about her work, the debts on his signature, his holding her hand at the end and taking the Book into his keeping.

upsert.boundary: Chalton Street, Somers Town: Hester's two rooms over a corn-chandler's, 1840 to 1884.
upsert.description: A working district north of the New Road, by the railway termini. Two rooms, a table at the window, ruled sheets, Kate's schoolbooks. Affords: piecework computing by parcel, sixpence a page, without a master in the room. Limit: the stairs, the light in winter, a widow's wage.

upsert.boundary: St James's Square: the Lovelaces' town house to 1846.
upsert.description: The London base of the first years of the Book; the engine's business is conducted from its morning room until the move to Great Cumberland Place.

upsert.boundary: Whitworth's works, Chorlton Street, Manchester, 1833 onward.
upsert.description: Whitworth's own firm: the true plane, measuring machines, the standard thread of 1841. Sends Enoch to London as fitter and erector, and in 1853 offers him a foremanship back at Chorlton Street, which he takes. Affords: standard gauges and men trained to them.

changes.value: Inner lives for the places, workshops, the three relationships and Britain: what each place affords and forbids, each relationship's phases, and the era's shocks that reach the story.

upsert.boundary: Ada's choice about her mother's loan, spring 1850.
upsert.description: Back in the business in January 1850, Ada reads Davies's statement with the Esher loan in red: £2,500 owed to Lady Byron, secured on the engine, so that if the trust fails the engine is her mother's. She wants the engine free of her mother before it is shown. How she sets about it is a choice among continuations.
provenance: invented: pass 3 decision, opened in answer to reader notes

answers.meaning: A mathematical system on the turf with a small syndicate (Crosse, Malcolm, Fleming), to pay her mother off from winnings; kept from William, Davies and Babbage, against the Book's own rule of nothing withheld.
She lets the loan stand and pays it from the tables' income over years, swallowing her mother's hold.
She asks William to pay it from the estate, making the engine's debt his.
She asks the offices to buy the loan out against future tables.

provenance: invented: proposal policy, declared before the draw; a_turf weighted by the historical pull of Ada's 1850-51 betting
upsert.question: What does Ada do about her mother's loan secured on the engine, once she is back in 1850?
upsert.unit: one unit of the modeler's proposal policy over continuations (not a forecast)

changes.value: Readers ask what Ada wants that the Book denies her, and what the August 1852 confession concerned. The model holds a live open choice the earlier pass never opened: once Ada is back in 1850, what does she do about her mother's £2,500 loan secured on the engine itself (Lady Byron's third condition, Nov 1847)? Historically Ada bet on the turf with a syndicate in 1850-51 and lost heavily at the 1851 Derby; the change gives that habit a new object. Declared before the draw.

upsert.boundary: Babbage's choice about his improvements to the printing section, spring 1848.
upsert.description: Ada is barred under her mother's conditions; Davies conducts from Lombard Street and comes to the shop twice a week. Babbage has redrawn the type-wheel train of the printing section so that it can print two columns at once. De Morgan's 1846 award freezes every drawing without a fresh award. What does he do with it?
provenance: invented: pass 3 decision, opened in answer to reader notes

answers.meaning: He has one of Clement's old men cut a trial train to the new drawing at night, unsigned, against the award; Enoch finds it.
He leaves the table engine alone and pours the improvement into the Analytical Engine drawings at night, as historically he did with Difference Engine No. 2 in 1847-49.
He asks De Morgan for a fresh award, properly.
He stays away from the shop for months.

provenance: invented: proposal policy, declared before the draw
upsert.question: With Ada barred, what does Babbage do with his redrawn type-wheel train?
upsert.unit: one unit of the modeler's proposal policy over continuations (not a forecast)

changes.value: Readers find Babbage's compulsion to improve dramatized once and then dissolved. The model has babbage.design_changes and the 1846 award freezing the drawings; with Ada barred from January 1848 and Davies conducting, nobody stands between Babbage and the shop but Enoch. What he does with his next improvement is an open choice. Declared before the draw.

upsert.description: The engine loses its advocate on the Guardian's board.
Without its maker the engine's condition falls and its attendance costs rise.
The attachment begun at Fyne Court is what she confesses.
The GRO engine's record of costly attendance turns actuaries against engines.
Henry's letter sets off William's decision and the invitation to Mrs Fell.
Checked hand tables become as safe as the engine's and cheaper.
The loan secured on the engine is what Ada wants paid off.
The sessions and the planted faults produce the Rule.

upsert.boundary: Ada at Fyne Court, Somerset, November 1844, where she meets John Crosse.
upsert.description: Ada stays with Andrew Crosse, the electrician, at Fyne Court on the Quantocks, and meets his son John, then in his twenties. Real history: the friendship that began here was close and lasted to her death, and John Crosse destroyed her letters afterwards. The change does not touch it.
provenance: source: Ada's 1844 visit to Fyne Court and her friendship with John Crosse are in the historical record

upsert.boundary: Babbage's nights at the Analytical Engine while Ada is barred, 1848-1849.
upsert.description: Realizes cut.dec.1848.babbage answer b_ae_only. He has redrawn the type-wheel train to print two columns at once; the award freezes the table engine, so he puts the idea into the Analytical Engine's printing drawings instead, working from ten at night, and leaves the shop alone. He comes to the shop less, and when he comes he talks to Enoch about the mill. Article the Second, which defers the great engine, is the one he keeps breaking in his head.
provenance: invented: realized draw b_ae_only (seed book-of-conditions/pass3/dec.1848.babbage/type-wheels); consistent with his historical work on DE2 and the AE in 1847-49

upsert.boundary: The working sessions in the sewing room and at Chalton Street, February to August 1848.
upsert.description: Two hours a day. Ada wants mathematics; Hester wants a check she can trust. Their first quarrel: Hester chooses ages to check as a careful clerk would (round ages, ends of columns); Ada wants them drawn by lot from a tea caddy. Then Hester's insight: difference the printed table back. Hester holds that differencing back is enough. Ada plants two faults in a copy without telling her: a slip at 53 carried forward, and a wrong starting third difference that leaves every difference smooth and every figure wrong. Hester's differencing finds the first and passes the second; twelve ages drawn by lot and computed fresh by the commutation road find the second at once. So the Rule needs both hands: differencing back for a fault in the machine's working, fresh figures at drawn ages for a fault in what it was given. Hester is wrong in front of a countess and does not forgive it for a week.
provenance: invented: pass 3, answering readers on the Rule's two kinds of error

upsert.boundary: Ada asks William to pay off her mother's loan, April 1850.
upsert.description: Realizes cut.dec.1850.loan answer c_william. At Ockham, Ada asks William for £2,500 to pay Lady Byron and free the engine from her mother's security; it is the first time she has asked him for anything before telling anyone else. He sells the oaks in the lower park and pays it in May. He will not have it written in the Book: he says a husband's money is not a condition. The Book stays silent on it, the one large transaction in the business with no article. Lady Byron is repaid, and loses the hold the security gave her.

upsert.boundary: Ada tells William something in August 1852 that makes him leave the room.
upsert.description: The model's answer (inferred from the historical record, where the likeliest reading is the same): she tells him of her attachment to John Crosse since 1844, and asks that a packet of his letters be returned to him unopened. William walks out without his hat and walks most of the night. The prose does not say what she told him; it shows the packet, and what the silence costs. His trust and closeness fall and do not recover; she turns to the Book, whose last article asks him to take it by gift.
provenance: inferred: pass 3 gives the confession content in the model; earlier passes left it unknown

upsert.boundary: The General Register Office's Scheutz engine, built by Bryan Donkin, 1859.
upsert.description: Real history: a copy of the Scheutz difference engine is built in London for the General Register Office and used for William Farr's English Life Table (1864), with much hand checking; it is little used after. In this world it is the second working table engine in Britain, and its record of costly attendance and checking is read by every actuary.
provenance: source: the Donkin-built Scheutz engine for the GRO (1859) and Farr's English Life Table (1864)

upsert.boundary: The Institute of Actuaries adopts a rule for checking tables, 1866.
upsert.description: The Institute's council adopts, for the tables its members compute and publish, a rule of differencing back by an independent hand and fresh computation at arguments drawn by lot. It calls it the Rule of Two Hands and names no source. Hand tables checked this way are now as safe as the engine's and cheaper.
provenance: invented: pass 3; the Institute of Actuaries itself is real (founded 1848)

upsert.boundary: Henry Babbage writes to Lord Lovelace about 'the green book at Horsley', November 1877.
upsert.description: Sorting his father's papers, Henry finds Ada's initials in the corners of the 1845 drawings and a note in his father's hand, 'the green book is at Horsley; it is hers and his now'. He writes asking whether it exists and whether he may see it, since the engine is his. William, seventy-two and lately ill, has a reason and a recipient at once; Henry's letter names Mrs Fell as the computer, still living.
provenance: invented: pass 3, to motivate the date of the coda

changes.value: Pass 3: realize the two drawn decisions, open the Rule sessions into their two kinds of error and Hester's mistake, give the confession its content in the model, and add the world events that explain why the Guardian gave up its engine in 1867 and why William acted in 1878.

Pass 3: give the processes that held only a starting value their courses across each life, turning at the Events that move them. Real-life dates follow the historical record; values on authored scales are sketches with the anchors each process declares.

upsert.boundary: Ada at Fyne Court, Somerset, November 1844, where she meets John Crosse.
upsert.description: Ada stays with Andrew Crosse, the electrician, at Fyne Court on the Quantocks, and meets his son John, then in his twenties. Real history: the friendship that began here was close and lasted to her death, and John Crosse destroyed her letters afterwards. The change does not touch it.
provenance: source: Ada's 1844 visit to Fyne Court and her friendship with John Crosse are in the historical record

upsert.boundary: Babbage's nights at the Analytical Engine while Ada is barred, 1848-1849.
upsert.description: Realizes cut.dec.1848.babbage answer b_ae_only. He has redrawn the type-wheel train to print two columns at once; the award freezes the table engine, so he puts the idea into the Analytical Engine's printing drawings instead, working from ten at night, and leaves the shop alone. He comes to the shop less, and when he comes he talks to Enoch about the mill. Article the Second, which defers the great engine, is the one he keeps breaking in his head.
provenance: invented: realized draw b_ae_only (seed book-of-conditions/pass3/dec.1848.babbage/type-wheels); consistent with his historical work on DE2 and the AE in 1847-49

upsert.boundary: The working sessions in the sewing room and at Chalton Street, February to August 1848.
upsert.description: Two hours a day. Ada wants mathematics; Hester wants a check she can trust. Their first quarrel: Hester chooses ages to check as a careful clerk would (round ages, ends of columns); Ada wants them drawn by lot from a tea caddy. Then Hester's insight: difference the printed table back. Hester holds that differencing back is enough. Ada plants two faults in a copy without telling her: a slip at 53 carried forward, and a wrong starting third difference that leaves every difference smooth and every figure wrong. Hester's differencing finds the first and passes the second; twelve ages drawn by lot and computed fresh by the commutation road find the second at once. So the Rule needs both hands: differencing back for a fault in the machine's working, fresh figures at drawn ages for a fault in what it was given. Hester is wrong in front of a countess and does not forgive it for a week.
provenance: invented: pass 3, answering readers on the Rule's two kinds of error

upsert.boundary: Ada asks William to pay off her mother's loan, April 1850.
upsert.description: Realizes cut.dec.1850.loan answer c_william. At Ockham, Ada asks William for £2,500 to pay Lady Byron and free the engine from her mother's security; it is the first time she has asked him for anything before telling anyone else. He sells the oaks in the lower park and pays it in May. He will not have it written in the Book: he says a husband's money is not a condition. The Book stays silent on it, the one large transaction in the business with no article. Lady Byron is repaid, and loses the hold the security gave her.

upsert.boundary: Ada tells William something in August 1852 that makes him leave the room.
upsert.description: The model's answer (inferred from the historical record, where the likeliest reading is the same): she tells him of her attachment to John Crosse since 1844, and asks that a packet of his letters be returned to him unopened. William walks out without his hat and walks most of the night. The prose does not say what she told him; it shows the packet, and what the silence costs. His trust and closeness fall and do not recover; she turns to the Book, whose last article asks him to take it by gift.
provenance: inferred: pass 3 gives the confession content in the model; earlier passes left it unknown

upsert.boundary: The General Register Office's Scheutz engine, built by Bryan Donkin, 1859.
upsert.description: Real history: a copy of the Scheutz difference engine is built in London for the General Register Office and used for William Farr's English Life Table (1864), with much hand checking; it is little used after. In this world it is the second working table engine in Britain, and its record of costly attendance and checking is read by every actuary.
provenance: source: the Donkin-built Scheutz engine for the GRO (1859) and Farr's English Life Table (1864)

upsert.boundary: The Institute of Actuaries adopts a rule for checking tables, 1866.
upsert.description: The Institute's council adopts, for the tables its members compute and publish, a rule of differencing back by an independent hand and fresh computation at arguments drawn by lot. It calls it the Rule of Two Hands and names no source. Hand tables checked this way are now as safe as the engine's and cheaper.
provenance: invented: pass 3; the Institute of Actuaries itself is real (founded 1848)

upsert.boundary: Henry Babbage writes to Lord Lovelace about 'the green book at Horsley', November 1877.
upsert.description: Sorting his father's papers, Henry finds Ada's initials in the corners of the 1845 drawings and a note in his father's hand, 'the green book is at Horsley; it is hers and his now'. He writes asking whether it exists and whether he may see it, since the engine is his. William, seventy-two and lately ill, has a reason and a recipient at once; Henry's letter names Mrs Fell as the computer, still living.
provenance: invented: pass 3, to motivate the date of the coda

upsert.boundary: The Book locked in William's desk at Horsley, November 1852 to April 1878.
upsert.description: Given to William by Ada when dying, with the charge to read every page and do what he thought right. He reads it over three evenings in December 1852 and for twenty-five years does nothing with it, because he does not know what is right.

upsert.boundary: Britain, 1843 to 1852: railway mania, the panic of 1847, cholera, the Exhibition.
upsert.description: Railway mania 1845 to 1846 draws capital away from everything else; the commercial crisis of 1847 and the Bank Act suspended on 25 October 1847; cholera in London 1848 to 1849; the Great Exhibition 1851 with the table engine in the Machinery Court. Life offices multiply and need tables. The era's money is cheap and then suddenly dear, and the engine's subscription lives inside that swing.

upsert.boundary: The Guardian as the engine's keeper, 1852 to 1867.
upsert.description: The office takes the table engine when the trust can no longer carry it, prints its tables under the Rule of Two Hands with Hester as second hand, and gives it up in 1867 for the Institute of Actuaries' hand-computed tables, back to Henry Babbage. It keeps Hester computing three days a week into the 1870s.

upsert.boundary: Ada and her mother: the three conditions, November 1847 to Ada's death.
upsert.description: Lady Byron hears the whole of the shortfall, asks eleven exact questions, goes through the ledger with her finger, and offers money on three written conditions pasted into the Book with her initials. Her help is real and is control: the relationship's lifelong form, now on paper. In 1850 William pays her off and the paper hold ends; in 1852 she takes the sickroom in hand.

upsert.boundary: Ada and Babbage under the Book, 1843 to 1852.
upsert.description: Phases: negotiation (autumn 1843, articles argued word by word); partnership and quarrel (1845 to 1846, the redesign quarrel, Ada's anger, De Morgan's award); her withdrawal (1848) and return (1850); he is not asked to come when she is dying (1852). Each holds something the other needs and cannot command: his engine, her business. The Book is how they trust without trusting.

upsert.boundary: Chalton Street, Somers Town: Hester's two rooms over a corn-chandler's, 1840 to 1884.
upsert.description: A working district north of the New Road, by the railway termini. Two rooms, a table at the window, ruled sheets, Kate's schoolbooks. Affords: piecework computing by parcel, sixpence a page, without a master in the room. Limit: the stairs, the light in winter, a widow's wage.

upsert.boundary: The subscription's shortfall, April to November 1847.
upsert.description: Davies, going through the ledger with the subscription book and Enoch's weekly returns, makes the shortfall to the finish about £1,400 before the panic and about £2,400 after it. Failure mode: the subscribers are themselves life offices whose funds the panic squeezes, so the money fails exactly when it is needed. Ada knows the £1,400 from April and tells no one.

upsert.boundary: The table engine's calculating section, cut and erected at Dorset Street, May 1845 to September 1849.
upsert.description: Three columns of figure wheels, about 270 wheels in all, each gauged for pitch, bore, boss and thickness by a gauge that must enter and one that must not; from 1846 the anticipating carriage, which lifts every carry in a column at once and makes each turn of the handle about half as long again as fast. Capacity: a table to seven figures and third differences. Limit: a worn carry lever can take a carry it should not, only when the figures fall just so.

upsert.boundary: The worn carry lever on the sixth wheel, found July 1850.
upsert.description: Hester's differencing finds the third differences jump at age 71; Enoch traces it to a bright flat on the lever's nose, no wider than a hair, worn by ten thousand turns. The lever had passed the gauge a year before; the steel wore. The failure mode the Rule of Two Hands exists to catch.

upsert.boundary: Whitworth's works, Chorlton Street, Manchester, 1833 onward.
upsert.description: Whitworth's own firm: the true plane, measuring machines, the standard thread of 1841. Sends Enoch to London as fitter and erector, and in 1853 offers him a foremanship back at Chorlton Street, which he takes. Affords: standard gauges and men trained to them.

upsert.boundary: Horsley Towers, 4 April 1878: William gives the Book of Conditions to Henry Prevost Babbage after Hester Fell has checked its tables.
upsert.description: Set off by Henry's letter of November 1877. William, seventy-three, asks Hester, sixty-six, to check the tables in the Book before he gives it away. She differences Table I back, draws twelve ages, and finds her own name in two articles, never having seen the Book. William turns back to Lady Byron's sheet, then initials the space beside Article the Last, W.L., 4th April 1878, and gives the Book to Henry. On the train home Hester writes Differenced, H.F. at the foot of her sheet.

Seed 'autumn' (the falling season, harvest, the fall): Hester Fell, from fell as the old word for falling and a northern surname; Martha Fallows, from fallow fields; Harriet Russet, from the autumn colour, rejected because it is too decorative. Selected: Hester Fell, plain and short, Hester an ordinary 1810s name, no initial shared with Ada or Annabella. Seed 'dusk': Enoch Dunn, from dun, the dusky brown, with Enoch a common Methodist Lancashire name; Samuel Dimmock, from dim; Abel Gloam, rejected as forced. Selected: Enoch Dunn. These are invented derivations, not etymologies of the real surnames.","data":{"tasks":[{"taskHash":"5f713fbe0448f22f751337fc5354946f13e57b7d1b2f8be8e296245cb580ba67","seed":"autumn","alternatives":["Hester Fell","Martha Fallows","Harriet Russet"],"selected":"Hester Fell"},{"taskHash":"ab137781cb40c547e869fb6a585ff2574f8bd521aa3e02500628bf6e6670d397","seed":"dusk","alternatives":["Enoch Dunn","Samuel Dimmock","Abel Gloam"],"selected":"Enoch Dunn"}]},"authoringClock":{"rootId":"story.understanding.c478361e6869af25970682a2","unit":"authoring_step","at":1}}

upsertNodes.text: {"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"decision","text":"D1 (u=0.396, b_table_engine): the work is a finishable table engine for the life offices, with the Analytical Engine postponed to a second article. D2 (u=0.561, b_dorset_shop): it is built behind Babbage's house under his eye, with Clement's planer and a foreman lent by Whitworth, so the struggle over finishing moves inside the shop. D3 (u=0.292, b_mother): in the 1847 shortfall Ada accepts her mother's written conditions, so the woman who wrote the Book of Conditions is herself put under conditions and withdrawn for two years. Kept: all three draws without reroll. Chapter route (coarse): 1 the morning, 2 Article the First, 3 Prospect Place, 4 the deed, 5 piecework (Hester), 6 the shop (Enoch), 7 Article the Third, 8 the panic and the mother, 9 the Rule of Two Hands, 10 the first table, 11 the last article, 12 coda. D4 (the Exhibition) and D5 (the Book's fate) will be drawn when the model reaches 1851-52."}
upsertNodes.title: What the three draws make of the branch

upsertNodes.text: {"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"interpretation","text":"Aimscatter#ded3 holds for Babbage before 1843: the Difference Engine, the Analytical Engine, cipher-breaking, lighthouse signals, the Decline of Science quarrel and his Saturday soirees all draw on one supply of attention, and none advanced after 1834. Its condition is several directions competing for one capacity. Draw D2 put the shop behind his own house, which predicts the pattern returning inside the one project: redesign competing with execution. The model shows it at ev.1846.redesign_quarrel. The pattern's caution (person read as cause) applies: the dispersal comes from the structure of an inventor with no external deadline and private means, not from low ability. ScopeFreeze#548e is the counter-mechanism, and Article the Third of the Book of Conditions is a ScopeFreeze with De Morgan as the exception_policy (CostAnalysis). Its failure mode, the perfectionism spiral, is what the award of May 1846 partly concedes, allowing the carriage and freezing the rest."}
upsertNodes.title: Babbage's dispersal and the shop eleven steps away

upsertNodes.text: {"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"interpretation","text":"Focalpeer#3724: the subscription's joint action (offices paying, Davies canvassing, Babbage designing, Enoch cutting) comes to depend on Ada, who holds no assigned coordinating authority in law: the deed names her only in a schedule. Prediction from the pattern: if she withdraws, the action falters or changes. The model tests this at ev.1848.ada_withdraws: Davies keeps the money moving, but design discipline slips (Babbage's visits to the shop rise, the umpire is called less). The caution matters for the prose: the members have their own reasons (Davies's want for verified tables, Babbage's for the engine), so the book should not make Ada the sole author of the engine."}
upsertNodes.title: Ada as the focal member without authority

upsertNodes.text: {"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"hypothesis","text":"Identitylag#2fbd predicts that Hester, whose self-description is anchored to 'a computer who is paid by the page and replaceable', keeps acting as if her work were a commodity after the Rule of Two Hands and the first table make her the engine's verifier. Predicted observable: she undercharges and defers in 1848-1851 while her standing rises from 3 to 6. Babbage shows the mirror case: his self-description as the neglected inventor persists after the engine runs."}
upsertNodes.title: Hester's self-understanding lags her standing

upsertNodes.text: {"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"foundation","text":"Concept: a human life in this world. Purpose: to follow how each of the fourteen people changes from birth to death, and what the engine business does to them. Range: every person in the story, 1779 to 1918, from a Welsh slate-country boy to a countess. Carve (ConceptualDecomposition#d0fc, tests from DecompositionGate#1b2d): the nine slow processes, kept as the fixed top, each given a real unit or an anchored 0-10 scale: body (health), kin (count of living close kin), partnership (closeness), work (hours a week), place (belonging), means (pounds a year at one's own disposal), knowledge (skill in the main domain), standing (in one's own group), meaning (purpose). Routing sample (RoutingSanityCheck#71bd), frozen before values: Ada's pin money under coverture routes to means; Hester's piecework pages route to work; Babbage's loss of his mother routes to kin; Davies's FRS routes to standing. Each found one home. Warning kept: 'means' for married women measures money at her own disposal, not household wealth, so Ada's flat £300 is a fact about the law, not about the Lovelaces."}
upsertNodes.title: Claim frame for the person carve

upsertNodes.text: {"schema":"meaning-model-story-author-record/v1","kind":"author_model","text":"Fictional author persona, invented under delegation (no real author model supplied): Margaret Ellery Vane, b. 1961, a former life-office actuary in Edinburgh who left the profession at fifty to write. She writes this novel in 2026, at sixty-five, after nursing her mother through a long illness and reading Lovelace's letters during it. Her reasons, multiple and partly conflicting: affection for the actuarial craft she left; a wish to imagine a woman given the office Lovelace asked for, without pretending the law of the day allowed it; and the pleasure of machinery. Her voice: plain declarative prose, documents quoted as documents, a habit of counting, restraint at moments of feeling, images of tolerance and error.","data":{"schema":"meaning-model-story-author-model/v1","modeledAuthorId":"persona.vane","mode":"fictional_author","label":"Margaret Ellery Vane (invented persona)","basis":[{"id":"b.actuary","kind":"invented","description":"Thirty years as a life-office actuary; Consequential choices: (1) 15 Aug 1843 Babbage reads Ada's letter and, instead of refusing, writes beside one condition 'this one we may discuss' (ev.1843.morning). (2) Article the First, Oct 1843: a finishable table engine for life offices, design frozen (dec.1843.terms). (3) Jan 1844 Ada visits the dying Clement at Prospect Place, who tells her the tools were the quarrel and the drawings the disease (ev.1844.clement_visit; Clement dies 28 Feb). (4) June 1844 the deed: Davies and De Morgan trustees, William guarantor, Ada only in a schedule because coverture forbids her to contract (ev.1844.deed). (5) Oct 1844 Hester Pratt hired to verify hand tables (ev.1844.hester_hired). (6) Spring 1845 the Dorset Street shop with Clement's planer bought from his estate, Whitworth tools, Enoch lent as foreman (dec.1845.maker). (7) Mar-May 1846 Babbage's redesign; De Morgan's award: carriage allowed, rest frozen, waste charged to Babbage (ev.1846.redesign_quarrel). (8) Oct 1847 the panic, a £2,400 shortfall; Ada accepts her mother's written conditions, withdraws for two years, Davies conducts (dec.1847.shortfall). (9) 1848-49 the Rule of Two Hands, cholera, calculating section runs Sept 1849, Airy inspects Nov 1849. (10) July 1850 first table; Hester's discrepancy at age 71; Enoch's worn carry lever; 1851 Machinery Court and medal in Babbage's name, jurors name Ada (dec.1851.exhibition). (11) Aug-Nov 1852: confession withheld; Article the Last gives William the Book by gift (dec.1852.book); Ada dies 27 Nov 1852. (12) Coda, spring 1878, Horsley: William gives Henry the Book; Hester present; what happened to everyone; Hester's refusal of Enoch in 1853 (dec.1853.hester_enoch) told in retrospect. Real lives changed and why: Clement (an invented final visit; death date kept); Davies (drawn into a trustee role he never held; death kept); Whitworth (supplies tools, lends a foreman); Airy (a second inspection reverses his 1842 view in part); William (guarantor; the gift); Lady Byron (the loan and conditions); Henry (receives the Book). No real death date moves.","authoringClock":{"rootId":"story.understanding.c478361e6869af25970682a2","unit":"authoring_step","at":16}}
